title: Closing thoughts and thanks
summary: Hug says one must love the music and is proud of his reputation; the interview closes.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Did you have anything you wanted to add, generally, to the content I brought out, or asked about, anything that you think is important in describing your playing, or your career, or any phase of it that I haven't learned more?

Well, I think, Charlie, that first of all, you really have to like what you're doing, which is most important. And I have liked music, I've liked jazz music all my life, been around many, many greats, and I feel quite flattered to be associated with these people. And I'm really, really proud of the reputation that I have around New Orleans as a Dixieland jazz piano player, or whatever they want to call me, ragtime. It's still jazz. And especially when they associate it with New Orleans, it's very flattering. And there's very little that I could add to it, excepting to say that I'm thankful that I'm still playing, that I've gone through the different phases, different styles, and that I'm still around.
Thank you. Thanks a lot. Thanks a lot. Thanks a lot.
